support.quote: The United States led a boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics, held in Moscow, to protest against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
After the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan, United States’ President Jimmy Carter called for a boycott of the Moskva Olympics if the Soviets did not withdraw before 20 February 1980.
The U.S. led 36 nations in boycotting the 1980 Olympics, held in Moscow, as a protest against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan in December 1979.
called for a boycott of the 1980 Moscow Olympics, and stepped up its aid to the Afghan insurgents

assessments.note: the boycott is listed among the Carter administration responses to the Soviet invasion

support.quote: Western media largely viewed the boycott as a retaliatory move in response to the American-led boycott of the 1980 Games.

assessments.note: official Soviet reason was athletes' security; retaliation is the generally accepted real motive (the article also discusses other motives)

support.quote: One reason undoubtedly is simple revenge, tit for tat.
The African/Guyanan boycott was in protest of a recent tour of South Africa by the New Zealand national rugby side
boycotted the Montreal Games when the International Olympic Committee (IOC) refused to ban New Zealand, after the New Zealand national rugby union team had toured South Africa earlier in 1976
The Netherlands, Spain, and, somewhat surprisingly, Switzerland withdrew in protest of the Soviet action.
At the 1956 Summer Olympics in Melbourne, the Soviet handling of the Hungarian uprising led to a boycott by Spain, the Netherlands, and Switzerland.
This was due to the country’s policy of apartheid and, in particular, its use of the policy in choosing its athletic teams, which is forbidden by International Olympic Committee (IOC) policy.
South Africa first entered the Winter Olympics in 1960, and that summer's games in Rome would be its last till the end of apartheid.
The United States led a boycott of the 1980 Summer Olympics, held in Moscow, to protest against the Soviet invasion of Afghanistan.
